rules.statement: The Court has the power to set aside a sale order made without jurisdiction, and this can be done even if the property has been sold to a third party.
rules.supporting_quote: It seems to me that the contention for the appellant on this point must succeed. The Commissioner of Stamps has the power to make arrangements with regard to the payment of estate duty on such terms as he may think fit, and the property left by the deceased or donated by him is ordinarily not to be sold for the recovery of estate duty, unless it become impossible 179 to arrive at some arrangement with the executor or the donee. The Official Administrator as such has no more power than any other Administrator, and he has to apply for leave of Court to sell property even for the payment of the duty which has to be paid by him.

meta.parties: Samarasinghe v. Secretary District Court Matara
